abstract.name: Abstract
abstract.p: Recent work by Smagloy et al. (((ISIT 2020))) shows that the redundancy of a single-deletion s𝑠s-substitution correcting code is asymptotically at least (s+1)⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)𝑠1𝑛𝑜𝑛(s+1)\log n+o(\log n), where n𝑛n is the length of the codes. They also provide a construction of single-deletion and single-substitution codes with redundancy 6⁢log⁡n+86𝑛86\log n+8. In this paper, we propose a family of systematic single-deletion s𝑠s-substitution correcting codes of length n𝑛n with asymptotical redundancy at most (3⁢s+4)⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)3𝑠4𝑛𝑜𝑛(3s+4)\log n+o(\log n) and polynomial encoding/decoding complexity, where s≥2𝑠2s\geq 2 is a constant. Specifically, the encoding and decoding complexity of the proposed codes are O⁢(ns+3)𝑂superscript𝑛𝑠3O\left(n^{s+3}\right) and O⁢(ns+2)𝑂superscript𝑛𝑠2O\left(n^{s+2}\right), respectively.

document.keywords: Error-correcting codes, deletions, insertions, substitutions, systematic codes.

para.p: The problem of constructing deletion/insertion correcting codes was introduced by Levenshtein [1] and recently has attracted an increasing attention due to their relevance to the DNA-based data storage [2]. In [1], Levenshtein proved that a code can correct up to t𝑡t deletions if and only if it can correct up to t𝑡t insertions, if and only if it can correct the combination of t1subscript𝑡1t_{1} insertions and t2subscript𝑡2t_{2} deletions for any non-negative integers t1subscript𝑡1t_{1} and t2subscript𝑡2t_{2} such that t1+t2≤tsubscript𝑡1subscript𝑡2𝑡t_{1}+t_{2}\leq t. Levenshtein also proved that for any t𝑡t-deletion correcting code 𝒞𝒞\mathscr{C} of length n𝑛n, the redundancy of 𝒞(\mathscr{C}~(defined as n−log|𝒞|)n-\log|\mathscr{C}|) is asymptotically at least t⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)𝑡𝑛𝑜𝑛t\log n+o(\log n), and an optimal t𝑡t-deletion correcting code has redundancy at most 2⁢t⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)2𝑡𝑛𝑜𝑛2t\log n+o(\log n).
The first class of optimal single-deletion correcting codes, whose redundancy is log⁡n+O⁢(1)𝑛𝑂1\log n+O(1), are the well-known Varshamov-Tenengolts (VT) codes [3], which are defined as

A decoding algorithm of the VT codes to correct a single deletion was proposed in [1], and a systematic encoding algorithm of the VT codes was proposed in [4], both have linear-time complexity.

The VT construction was generalized in [5] and [6] by replacing the weight vector v=(1,2,…,n)v12…𝑛\textbf{v}=(1,2,\ldots,n) in the parity check equation with a t𝑡t-order recursive sequence. The resulted codes are capable of correcting t𝑡t deletions. However, the asymptotic rate of such codes is bounded away from 111.

Multiple-deletion correcting codes with small asymptotical redundancy were studied in several recent works. In [7], Brakensiek et al. presented a family of t𝑡t-deletion correcting codes with asymptotical redundancy O⁢(t2⁢log⁡t⁢log⁡n)𝑂superscript𝑡2𝑡𝑛O(t^{2}\log t\log n). For t=2𝑡2t=2, the redundancy was improved by the works of Gabrys et al. [8] and Sima et al. [9]. Specifically, the code in [8] has redundancy 8⁢log⁡n+O⁢(log⁡log⁡n)8𝑛𝑂𝑛8\log n+O(\log\log n) and the code in [9] has redundancy 7⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)7𝑛𝑜𝑛7\log n+o(\log n). In a more recent work by Guruswami and Håstad [10], an explicit construction of 222-deletion correcting codes with redundancy 4⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)4𝑛𝑜𝑛4\log n+o(\log n) was proposed, which matches the existential upper bound of the optimal codes. However, it is not known that whether 4⁢log⁡n4𝑛4\log n corresponds to the redundancy of the optimal code, and it could be a⁢log⁡n𝑎𝑛a\log n, where a=2,3𝑎23a=2,3 or 444. For general t𝑡t, Sima and Bruck generalized the construction in [9] to t𝑡t-deletion correcting codes with redundancy 8⁢t⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)8𝑡𝑛𝑜𝑛8t\log n+o(\log n) [11], where n𝑛n is the number of information bits, and by further generalizing and applying the techniques in [11], Sima et al. provided a family of systematic t𝑡t-deletion correcting codes with 4⁢t⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)4𝑡𝑛𝑜𝑛4t\log n+o(\log n) bits of redundancy and O⁢(n2⁢t+1)𝑂superscript𝑛2𝑡1O(n^{2t+1}) encoding//decoding complexity [12].

However, in many application scenarios, such as DNA data storage and file synchronization, it is necessary to correct the edit errors (i.e., the combination of insertions, deletions and substitutions), which motivates the problem of constructing codes that can correct insertions, deletions and/or substitutions. A modified VT construction with redundancy log⁡n+O⁢(1)𝑛𝑂1\log n+O(1) was presented in [1] to correct a single insertion, deletion or substitution, which is also referred to as an edit. Quaternary codes that can correct a single edit for DNA data storage were considered in [13]. In [14], a family of single-deletion single-substitution correcting codes (i.e., codes that can correct a single deletion and a single substitution simultaneously) with redundancy 6⁢log⁡n+86𝑛86\log n+8 was constructed using four VT-like parity check equations. The codes constructed in [12] are capable of correcting combination of insertions, deletions and substitutions such that the total number of insertions, deletions and substitutions is upper bounded by k𝑘k. Such codes have redundancy 4⁢k⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)4𝑘𝑛𝑜𝑛4k\log n+o(\log n), which is the best known construction with respect to redundancy.

In this paper, we study the problem of constructing single-deletion s𝑠s-substitution correcting codes, i.e., codes that can correct the combination of a single deletion and up to s𝑠s substitutions. It was shown by Smagloy et.al. in [14] that the redundancy r𝑟r of such codes satisfies

para.p: The main result of this paper is a construction of a family of single-deletion s𝑠s-substitution correcting codes with a systematic encoding function and with redundancy r𝑟r satisfying

Math.text: r <= (3 * s + 4) * logarithm@(n) + o * logarithm@(n)

para.p: The encoding and decoding complexity of the proposed codes are O⁢(ns+3)𝑂superscript𝑛𝑠3O\left(n^{s+3}\right) and O⁢(ns+2)𝑂superscript𝑛𝑠2O\left(n^{s+2}\right), respectively. On the other hand, systematic codes are desirable in practice since the information sequence can be extracted directly from a codeword during decoding.

Similar higher order weight vectors are used in the construction of single-deletion single-substitution correcting codes [14] and the construction of t𝑡t-deletion correcting codes [11], [12]. We prove that it is possible to use less redundancies (((than that used in [14] and [12]))) to construct single-deletion multiple-substitution correcting codes. According to the construction in [12], there exist codes correcting a single deletion and s𝑠s substitutions with redundancy 4⁢(s+1)⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)4𝑠1𝑛𝑜𝑛4(s+1)\log n+o(\log n). In this work, by using a pre-coding function of BCH code, our construction achieves the redundancy of (3⁢s+4)⁢log⁡n+o⁢(log⁡n)3𝑠4𝑛𝑜𝑛(3s+4)\log n+o(\log n), decreasing by s⁢log⁡n𝑠𝑛s\log n. The redundancy of our construction is s⁢log⁡n𝑠𝑛s\log n less than that the best known deletion//substitution correcting codes.

The key improvement of our construction is a pre-coding process using the BCH codes, i.e., the function hℎh constructed by Lemma 2. This technique can also be generalized to the construction of t𝑡t-deletion s𝑠s-substitution correcting codes for t>1𝑡1t>1. In fact, for each information sequence x, although the pre-coding process increases the redundancy by s⁢log⁡n𝑠𝑛s\log n, it decreases by a factor of nssuperscript𝑛𝑠n^{s} the number of vectors distinct from x which are “indistinguishable” with x in the presence of t𝑡t deletions and s𝑠s substitutions. Then a decrease of 2⁢s⁢log⁡n2𝑠𝑛2s\log n can be achieved by using the syndrome compression technique [15] with h⁢(x)ℎxh(\textbf{x}). Therefore, the overall redundancy decreases by s⁢log⁡n𝑠𝑛s\log n compared to the construction in [12]. Note that the codes constructed in [12] are capable of correcting any combination of insertions, deletions and substitutions, provided that the total number of deletions, insertions, and substitutions is not greater than t𝑡t, while in this paper, deletions and substitutions are handled separately, i.e., the codes are capable of correcting at most t𝑡t deletions and s𝑠s substitution, which makes it possible to decrease the number of “indistinguishable” sequences by the pre-coding process and hence decease the redundancy of the resulted codes.

Using a similar approach of pre-coding we can obtain an explicit construction of t𝑡t-deletion correcting codes whose redundancy is (4⁢t−1)⁢log⁡n4𝑡1𝑛(4t-1)\log n (improved by log⁡n𝑛\log n compared to the construction in [12]). Another possible line of research is nonbinary t𝑡t-deletion s𝑠s-substitution correcting codes. For nonbinary case, we can use codes from [16] for the pre-coding process.
